sections.title: Byte_Table_Access_Granularity
sections.summary:
# 5.3 Byte Table Access Granularity

**Section ID**: 5.3 | **Page**: 98-98

This section defines extensions to [2] to allow a Storage Device to report restrictions on byte table access alignment. While the general architecture permits writing data to byte tables at any byte boundary and with any length, some Storage Devices perform better when data is aligned to larger block boundaries. The section specifies how a device reports these alignment requirements via the `Set` method.

**Key Points**:
- **Alignment Requirements**: The Storage Device may enforce alignment constraints on byte table access.
- **Reporting Mechanism**: The device communicates its alignment requirements through the `Set` method invocation.
- **Purpose**: Enhances performance by ensuring data writes align to device-optimized block boundaries.

sections.title: Table_Table_Modification
sections.summary:
# 5.3.1 Table Table Modification

This section specifies additional columns to the **Table** table to report data alignment restrictions for byte tables. These restrictions apply only to byte tables, not Object tables.

### Key Requirements:
- The **Table** table SHALL include the additional columns listed in **Table 50**.
- The **MandatoryWriteGranularity** and **RecommendedAccessGranularity** columns are used to define alignment constraints.

### Table 50 - Table Table Additional Columns

| Column Number | Column Name | IsUnique | Column Type   |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 0x0D | MandatoryWriteGranularity | | uinteger_4 |
| 0x0E | RecommendedAccessGranularity | | uinteger_4 |

sections.title: MandatoryWriteGranularity
sections.summary:
# 5.3.1.1 MandatoryWriteGranularity

The **MandatoryWriteGranularity** column reports the granularity (in bytes) enforced by the Storage Device when the host invokes the `Set` method on byte tables. This column is **non-modifiable** by the host.

## 5.3.1.1.1 Object_Tables

For **object tables**, the **MandatoryWriteGranularity** value **SHALL be zero**.

## 5.3.1.1.2 Byte_Tables

For **byte tables**, the **MandatoryWriteGranularity** indicates the mandatory access granularity (in bytes) for the `Set` method. It defines the alignment requirement for:
- The **start offset (Where parameter)**
- The **length (Values parameter)**

### Requirements:
- The value of **MandatoryWriteGranularity** SHALL be **≤ RecommendedAccessGranularity** in the same row.
- The value SHALL be **≤ 8192**.
- If **ValidMandatoryGranularity** is **False**, the `Set` method SHALL fail with **INVALID PARAMETER**.
- If the TPer has no mandatory alignment requirement, **MandatoryWriteGranularity** SHALL be set to **1**.

### ValidMandatoryGranularity Criteria:
Valid if:
- **(x mod MandatoryWriteGranularity) = 0**
- **(y mod MandatoryWriteGranularity) = 0**

Where:
- **x** = start offset of the `Set` method (value of the **Where** parameter)
- **y** = number of data bytes being set (length of the **Values** parameter)

sections.title: RecommendedAccessGranularity
sections.summary:
### 5.3.1.2 RecommendedAccessGranularity

#### 5.3.1.2.1 Object_Tables
- The `RecommendedAccessGranularity` column reports the recommended granularity for host access to object tables via the `Set` or `Get` method.
- This column **SHALL NOT be modifiable by the host**.
- For rows in the `Table` table that pertain to object tables, the `RecommendedAccessGranularity` **SHALL be zero**.

#### 5.3.1.2.2 Byte_Tables
- For rows in the `Table` table that pertain to byte tables, the `RecommendedAccessGranularity` column indicates the **recommended access granularity in bytes** for the `Set` and `Get` methods.
- It reflects the **alignment** of data that enables optimal performance.
- If the TPer (Transport Provider) does not have a recommended alignment, the `RecommendedAccessGranularity` **SHALL be set to one**.
- When the host invokes the `Set` method on a byte table:
  - If `ValidRecommendedGranularity` (see Figure 5) is **False**, performance **MAY be reduced**.
- When the host invokes the `Get` method on a byte table:
  - If `ValidRecommendedGranularity` (see Figure 6) is **False**, performance **MAY be reduced**.
